html:
A South African singer, known as Mama Africa, who brought the music of southern Africa to the world and campaigned against apartheid for decades.

She began singing with jazz groups in Johannesburg in the 1950s. A role in the anti-apartheid film Come Back, Africa took her to Venice in 1959, and from there to the United States, where Harry Belafonte helped launch her career. When she tried to go home in 1960 for her mother's funeral, the government barred her return. She stayed in exile for thirty years.

  • Her hits included Pata Pata and "The Click Song", sung in Xhosa.
  • In 1963 she spoke against apartheid at the United Nations.
  • In 1966 she shared a Grammy award with Belafonte.

Her marriage to the Black Power activist Stokely Carmichael in 1968 cost her bookings in America, and she moved to Guinea. Nelson Mandela persuaded her to come home in 1990. She died in Italy in 2008, after singing at a concert.
